messages:
alex: Heads-up — saw a noticeable p95/p99 latency bump around 21:07 UTC after yesterday's RNG jitter change. Micro-batch timing looks much noisier on the heatmaps. Anyone else?

sophia: yup, I noticed it on the per-core tails. It lines up with the kernel anchoring tweak for long sequences. KV hit rate also dropped ~6% for the affected queues :frowning: 

raj: That was my deployment — kernel v2.1 landed which biases toward fused-attn for seq_len > 1k to avoid slow attention kernels. I didn't expect the scheduler jitter distribution to interact so badly.

perf-bot: Profiling summary (short): scheduling_tail +18ms on GPU-3, coalesce_delay distribution changed from {median:3ms, 95th:6ms} to {median:4ms, 95th:11ms}. KV: global miss rate +5.8%. Hotspot: queue group id=42.

alex: Can you paste the active batching config for that rollout? I want to see micro-batch interval, coalesce_delay, and jitter settings.

raj: Here's what was pushed (from canary):
```json
{
  "micro_batch_interval_ms": 4,
  "coalesce_delay_ms": 6,
  "jitter": "uniform(0,2)",
  "token_budget_target": 2048,
  "kernel_policy": "anchored:v2.1"
}
```

sophia: Two quick hypotheses: 1) uniform jitter with that kernel policy creates aligned wakeups across requests, causing synchronized kernel swaps and KV churn; 2) token_budget_target interacting with coalesce_delay increases the chance of forming large batches that thrash the KV cache during kernel swaps.

raj: Agreed on 1. The anchoring step triggers a per-seq kernel state update which temporarily invalidates some per-GPU KV priming heuristics. If multiple requests coalesce immediately after swap, cache miss storm.

alex: Ops — can we roll back kernel v2.1 on a canary while we test parameter tweaks? Keep prod untouched for now.

ops-bot: rolled back kernel on canary-3 -> kernel:v2.0 at 3865432113. Canary-3 traffic rerouted, no downtime.

perf-bot: Quick experiment suggestion: try increasing micro_batch_interval to 6ms, reduce coalesce_delay to 4ms, and switch jitter to triangular(0,2) (mode at 1ms) to de-synchronize peaks. Also reduce token_budget_target to 1536 for the canary. Expected outcome: fewer simultaneous cache-invalidating batches, lower KV miss spike.

sophia: I'll run that canary with the param set and collect KV-miss traces + per-kernel swap logs. Plan: canary for 30m with 5% traffic, then compare 1h baselines.

raj: I'll add a temporary guard in kernel selection to avoid anchoring within 500ms of a coalesce event (soft throttle) so we don't swap kernels during expected batch formation windows. If it looks good we can make it a heur.

alex: Action items: @sophia run canary and post traces (KV and coalesce histograms). @raj add guard and a small canary for kernel selection. I'll create a perf test to replay recent request traces with both configs. Re-evaluate after 1h.

ops-bot: canary config pushed to canary-3 at 3865432120: {micro_batch_interval_ms:6, coalesce_delay_ms:4, jitter:"triangular(0,2,1)", token_budget_target:1536}.

alex: Thanks — keep updates short here. If we see any regression, immediate rollback.

sophia: Started trace capture. First 5min look: coalesce 95th down from 11ms -> 7ms on canary, KV miss trend flattening. Will post full graphs in 30m. :thumbsup:
